# Contributing to the Entire CLI

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Entire! We welcome contributions from everyone.

Please read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.

> **New to Entire?** See the [README](README.md) for setup and usage documentation.

---

## Before You Code: Discuss First

The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before writing code. Please **open an issue first** using our [issue templates](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/new/choose) and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation.

### Contribution Workflow

1. **Open an issue** describing the problem or feature
2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
6. **Maintainer review and merge**

---

## First-Time Contributors

**New to open source or to Entire?** Start with the [First-Time Contributors Guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md). It walks through the full path: finding an issue, forking, setting up your dev environment, opening a PR, and what to expect afterwards.

The rest of this document is the reference for ongoing contributors.

---

## Submitting Issues

All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.

For security-related issues, see the Security section below.

---

## Security

If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.

---

## Contributions & Communication

Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:

- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support

Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.


## How to Contribute


There are many ways to contribute:

- **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
- **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
- **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
- **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
- **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge


## Reporting Bugs

Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:

### Required Information

1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
2. **Operating system**
3. **Go version** - run `go version`

### What to Include

Please answer these questions in your bug report:

1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
2. **What did you expect to happen?**
3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues

---

## Local Setup

### Prerequisites

- **Go 1.26.x** - Check with `go version`
- **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`

### Clone and Install

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
cd cli

# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
mise trust

# Install dependencies (mise will install the correct Go version)
mise install

# Download Go modules
go mod download

# Build the CLI
mise run build

# Verify setup by running tests
mise run test
```

> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for detailed architecture and development reference.

---

## Making Changes

1. **Create a branch** for your changes:
   ```bash
   git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
   ```

2. **Make your changes** - follow the [Code Style](#code-style) guidelines

3. **Test your changes** - see [Testing](#testing)

4. **Commit** with clear, descriptive messages:
   ```bash
   git commit -m "Add feature: description of what you added"
   ```

---

## Code Style

Follow standard Go idioms and conventions. For detailed guidance, see the **Go Code Style** section in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

### Key Points

- **Error handling**: Handle all errors explicitly - don't leave them unchecked
- **Formatting**: Code must pass `gofmt` (run `mise run fmt`)
- **Linting**: Code must pass `golangci-lint` (run `mise run lint`)
- **Naming**: Use meaningful, descriptive names following Go conventions

---

## Testing

> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for complete testing documentation.

```bash
# Unit tests - always run before committing
mise run test

# Integration tests
mise run test:integration

# Full CI suite
mise run test:ci
```

Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.

---

## Creating an Agent


Entire supports two ways to create agents:

### 1. Claude Code Agent Personas (Markdown)

These are markdown files that define specialized behaviors for Claude Code (e.g., developer, reviewer, etc.).

- **Location:** `.claude/agents/`
- **Structure:**
   ```markdown
   ---
   name: my-agent
   description: What this agent does
   model: opus
   color: blue
   ---

   # Agent Name
   You are a **[Role]** with expertise in [domain].

   ## Core Principles
   - Principle 1
   - Principle 2

   ## Process
   1. Step 1
   2. Step 2

   ## Output Format
   How to structure responses...
   ```
- **To invoke:** Create a matching command in `.claude/commands/` that spawns the agent via the Task tool.
- **Examples:**
   - `.claude/agents/dev.md` - TDD Developer
   - `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` - Code Reviewer

### 2. Coding Agent Integrations (Go)

These are Go implementations that integrate Entire with different AI coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, etc.) using the Agent abstraction layer.

- **Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/`
- **Steps:**
   1. Implement the `Agent` interface in `agent/agent.go`
   2. Register your agent in the agent registry
   3. Add setup and hook configuration as needed
   4. Ensure session and checkpoint tracking is handled per the abstraction
- **Reference:** See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for architecture and code examples.

---

**Which should I use?**

- Use a persona markdown agent if you want to create a new role or workflow for Claude Code.
- Use a coding agent integration if you want to add support for a new AI coding tool or extend agent capabilities in the CLI.

---

## Submitting a Pull Request

### Before You Submit

- **Related issue exists and is approved** -- Your PR references an issue where a maintainer has acknowledged the approach. (Exceptions: documentation fixes, typo corrections, and `good-first-issue` items.)
- **Linting passes** -- Run `mise run lint` (includes golangci-lint, gofmt, gomod, shellcheck)
- **Tests pass** -- Run `mise run test` to verify your changes
- **Tests included** -- New Go code and functionality should have accompanying tests
- **Entire checkpoint trailers included** -- See [Using Entire While Contributing](#using-entire-while-contributing) below

PRs that skip these steps are likely to be closed without merge.

### Submitting

1. **Push** your branch to your fork
2. **Open a PR** against the `main` branch
3. **Describe your changes** -- Link the related issue, summarize what changed and what testing you did
4. **Address Copilot feedback** -- See [Responding to Automated Review](#responding-to-automated-review)
5. **Wait for maintainer review**

---

Co-pilot agent reviews every PR and provides feedback on code quality, potential bugs, and project conventions.

# Branch review: `fix-checkpoint-trailer-block`

**Verdict: request changes**

Scope: `main...fix-checkpoint-trailer-block` at `2d16b3666`, covering one commit and seven changed files.

## Author intent

The change separates two meanings that the old checkpoint parser conflated:

- Whole-message parsing remains available for historical discovery, especially GitHub and native Git squash commits containing several embedded checkpoint trailers.
- Final-trailer-block parsing authorizes checkpoint creation, reuse, and mutation.

That split is the right design. The hook and attach changes apply it in several important places without breaking the existing squash-resume tests. The implementation is not complete, however: two mutation paths still trust whole-message results, and the strict parser does not match Git's trailer grammar.

No pull request currently exists for this branch. The related [PR #2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168) remains open.

## Spec

### Act on

#### High: `checkpoint explain --commit ... --generate` can write to a body-selected checkpoint

[`runExplainAuto`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L617) and [`runExplainCommit`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L2994) still resolve commit linkage with whole-message `ParseCheckpoint`. When `--generate` is present, that ID reaches [`store.Write`](cmd/entire/cli/explain.go#L1095).

A commit body can therefore name an existing but unrelated checkpoint and cause:

```text
commit body
    -> ParseCheckpoint(existing ID)
    -> checkpoint explain --generate --force
    -> generateCheckpointSummary
    -> store.Write(existing ID)
```

This violates the recorded requirement to "prevent untrusted checkpoint-shaped commit-body text from being accepted in unsafe contexts."

Use final-block parsing when commit resolution leads to summary generation. Keep whole-message parsing only for read-only discovery. Add regressions for both explicit `--commit` and positional commit fallback.

#### Medium: legacy migration still lets body text authorize reconciliation

[`migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_migration.go#L72) scans the whole message when a legacy state lacks `LastCheckpointCommitHash`. A matching body ID advances both `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit`, skipping normal migration and changing future attribution.

This conflicts with the intended boundary that body IDs are discovery candidates while final-block IDs authorize mutation.

Require final-block evidence for the legacy fallback, or decline reconciliation when the recorded commit hash is unavailable. Add a legacy-state regression with a matching body ID followed by a different final trailer block.

### Consider

None.

### Noted

The existing squash-history semantics are preserved. All three named squash-resume unit tests passed unchanged.

### Dismissed

None.

**Worst spec issue:** `--generate` can persist a summary to a checkpoint selected solely by commit-body text.

## Standards

### Act on

#### High: leading whitespace turns body text into an authorizing trailer

[`ParseAllCheckpointsFromFinalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L162) and [`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L306) left-trim lines before classifying and parsing them.

This line is therefore accepted:

```text
  Entire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6
```

Git 2.50's `git interpret-trailers --parse` returns no trailer for the same message. The branch parser nevertheless lets that line choose the ID used by PostCommit condensation and attach.

Do not remove leading spaces or tabs when validating final-block trailer lines. Add production-path regressions for PostCommit and attach, not only parser tests.

#### Medium: commit-message comment handling does not follow Git configuration

[`parseCheckpointFromCommitMessageFile`](cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L290) strips only `#` suffix lines. Git permits a configurable `core.commentChar`, and default cleanup preserves comment-prefixed lines when no editor runs. See the official [`git commit` cleanup documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit/2.52.0).

This creates two failure shapes:

- A repository using another comment character can hide a legitimate final trailer behind Git's comment block.
- A `git commit -m` or `-F` message can contain real `#` user content that this helper discards before deciding an earlier checkpoint-shaped body line is final.

Resolve Git's effective comment character or apply Git-equivalent cleanup rules. Cover editor, `-m`/`-F`, and custom-comment-character flows.

### Consider

#### Support Git trailer continuations

[`finalTrailerBlock`](cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go#L317) walks backward only while every line independently matches `Key: value`. Git accepts continuation lines beginning with whitespace, so a multiline trailer after `Entire-Checkpoint` can make the branch parser reject the entire block even though Git accepts it.

This may produce a duplicate checkpoint ID during prepare/amend or make PostCommit skip condensation. Either support continuation lines or explicitly document and test the narrower grammar.

#### Exercise attach through its durable boundary

`TestAttachIgnoresCheckpointShapedBodyText` calls `resolveCheckpointID` and `promptAmendCommit` separately. It does not prove through `runAttach` that a forged checkpoint remains unmodified and a fresh checkpoint receives the attached session.

A full-path regression should inspect the persistent store after attach.

### Noted

- The strict maintainability pass found no structural regression. The large hook file was already over 1,000 lines; this change did not cross that threshold or scatter the core parser policy.
- The parser change adds no lock or interruption point. Parser selection occurs before existing writes, so cleanup and recovery semantics are otherwise unchanged.
- Median `PrepareCommitMsg` time was 15.20 ms on this branch versus 15.13 ms on `main`, a difference of roughly 0.5% and within sample noise.

### Dismissed

One adversarial reviewer flagged `hasUserContent` for treating every checkpoint-shaped line as Entire metadata. That behavior predates this branch and requires a commit whose only user content is itself checkpoint-shaped. It is not a regression introduced here.

**Worst standards issue:** the strict parser accepts a Git-invalid indented body line as mutation authority.

## Correctness model

### Who owns each write?

- PrepareCommitMsg chooses the checkpoint ID; PostCommit owns condensation into persistent checkpoint storage.
- Attach chooses or reuses an ID, writes the attached session, then best-effort amends the commit.
- `checkpoint explain --generate` owns summary persistence.
- Session migration owns `BaseCommit` and `AttributionBaseCommit` reconciliation.

The first two owners now use the strict parser in their main paths. Summary generation and legacy migration do not.

### What happens around interruption?

The diff changes classification before existing writes. It does not add a lock, subprocess, temporary file, or new partial-write state. Existing write and recovery owners remain responsible before and after the decision. The outstanding risk is wrong-target mutation, not new interruption behavior.

### Which tests observe the real contract?

- The PrepareCommitMsg regression enters the production hook and would fail on the old code.
- The attach test observes helpers rather than the durable store contract.
- No regression covers body-selected summary generation, legacy migration, indented pseudo-trailers, custom Git comment characters, or trailer continuation lines.

## Multi-model agreement

Three independent reviewers examined the same intent and diff:

| Finding | Agreement | Disposition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Explain generation trusts body IDs | 3/3 | Act on |
| Indented pseudo-trailer accepted | 2/3 | Act on |
| Legacy migration trusts body IDs | 2/3 | Act on |
| Git comment handling is hard-coded | 1/3 | Act on after local verification |
| `hasUserContent` removes body-shaped lines | 1/3 | Dismissed as pre-existing |

## Verification performed

- Focused trailer parser tests passed.
- Focused PrepareCommitMsg and attach tests passed.
- `TestFindCheckpointInHistory_MultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestFindBranchCheckpoint_SquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints` passed.
- `TestResumeFromCurrentBranch_MultipleCheckpointsSaysLatest` passed.
- `git diff --check main..HEAD` passed.
- Git 2.50 rejected indented pseudo-trailers and accepted continuation-line trailer blocks in direct `git interpret-trailers --parse` checks.
- Checkpoint history records a successful pre-commit `mise run check`; the full gate was not rerun during this read-only review.

## Recommendation

Request changes. Close the two remaining mutation paths first, then make the strict parser agree with Git about indentation and comment cleanup. Preserve whole-message discovery for squash history throughout.

## Problem

A shadow checkpoint's commit subject is built from text Entire does not author:

- `strategy.FormatIncrementalMessage(step.TodoContent, ...)` — the `content` of a TodoWrite item the model wrote, verbatim apart from a 60-rune truncation.
- `generateCommitMessage` → `cleanPromptForCommit` — the session's first prompt, verbatim apart from prefix trimming and a 72-rune truncation.

Neither strips newlines. That text is steerable by anything the agent read into its context, including a file in the repository it is working on.

`FormatShadowCommit` / `FormatShadowTaskCommit` write that subject, then a blank line, then the real trailers. The parsers in this package scanned the **whole message, unanchored, and took the first match** — and the subject comes first. So one newline in the subject was enough:

```
Refactored the parser
Entire-Metadata: ../../../../etc      <- injected
Entire-Session: attacker-session      <- injected

Entire-Metadata: .entire/metadata/<real>
Entire-Session: <real>
Entire-Strategy: manual-commit
```
```
ParseSession(msg)  -> "attacker-session"
ParseMetadata(msg) -> "../../../../etc"
```

This is not cosmetic. The forged values drive real decisions:

- `ephemeralStore.ListCheckpoints` (`checkpoint/ephemeral.go:544`) filters commits by `ParseSession`, so a forged session ID re-attributes a checkpoint to another session, or hides it from its own.
- `ReadEphemeral` (`checkpoint/ephemeral.go:206-207`) and `ListCheckpoints` (`:572`) return `ParseMetadata`'s value as the checkpoint's metadata directory.
- Manual-commit rewind (`strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go:343,497,560`) resolves *which session's shadow branch to reset* from `ParseSession`.

## Fix

Both halves are needed — I checked, and flattening alone does not close it. Collapsing the subject to one line still left `Entire-Session:` sitting mid-line, and the unanchored pattern matched it there, so the collapsed subject kept winning.

1. **Flatten** the subject and the trailer values onto single lines in both shadow formatters. Every call site already passes a single-line subject, so this is lossless for legitimate input. Values get the same treatment because a newline in one splices an extra trailer line into the block, and `ValidateSessionID` is a denylist that does not reject a newline.
2. **Anchor** the four trailer patterns to the start of a line (`(?m)^`). A git trailer is a line, not a substring; a key appearing inside prose was never a trailer.

## Not covered here

`FormatCheckpoint` embeds the user's (or agent's) real commit message, which is legitimately multi-line, so it cannot be flattened. Anchoring hardens it against mid-line mentions but a line-start `Entire-Checkpoint:` typed into a commit body still parses. Closing that needs scoping the reads to the final trailer block (as `HasOPFApplied` already does via `finalTrailerBlock`), which changes `ParseAllCheckpoints` semantics for squash merges — a separate call.

Three new tests in `trailer_forgery_test.go`, each failing on `main` and passing here. They assert the parsers return the real values and that the only lines *beginning* with a trailer key are the ones the formatter wrote.

The existing `"multiple trailers returns first"` case is unchanged (both trailers are in the real block).

```
Entire-Session: attacker-session      <- injected

Entire-Metadata: .entire/metadata/<real>
Entire-Session: <real>
Entire-Strategy: manual-commit
```
```
ParseSession(msg)  -> "attacker-session"
ParseMetadata(msg) -> "../../../../etc"
```

This is not cosmetic. The forged values drive real decisions:

- `ephemeralStore.ListCheckpoints` (`checkpoint/ephemeral.go:544`) filters commits by `ParseSession`, so a forged session ID re-attributes a checkpoint to another session, or hides it from its own.
- `ReadEphemeral` (`checkpoint/ephemeral.go:206-207`) and `ListCheckpoints` (`:572`) return `ParseMetadata`'s value as the checkpoint's metadata directory.
- Manual-commit rewind (`strategy/manual_commit_rewind.go:343,497,560`) resolves *which session's shadow branch to reset* from `ParseSession`.

## Fix

Both halves are needed — I checked, and flattening alone does not close it. Collapsing the subject to one line still left `Entire-Session:` sitting mid-line, and the unanchored pattern matched it there, so the collapsed subject kept winning.

1. **Flatten** the subject and the trailer values onto single lines in both shadow formatters. Every call site already passes a single-line subject, so this is lossless for legitimate input. Values get the same treatment because a newline in one splices an extra trailer line into the block, and `ValidateSessionID` is a denylist that does not reject a newline.
2. **Anchor** the four trailer patterns to the start of a line (`(?m)^`). A git trailer is a line, not a substring; a key appearing inside prose was never a trailer.

## Not covered here

`FormatCheckpoint` embeds the user's (or agent's) real commit message, which is legitimately multi-line, so it cannot be flattened. Anchoring hardens it against mid-line mentions but a line-start `Entire-Checkpoint:` typed into a commit body still parses. Closing that needs scoping the reads to the final trailer block (as `HasOPFApplied` already does via `finalTrailerBlock`), which changes `ParseAllCheckpoints` semantics for squash merges — a separate call.

## Tests

Three new tests in `trailer_forgery_test.go`, each failing on `main` and passing here. They assert the parsers return the real values and that the only lines *beginning* with a trailer key are the ones the formatter wrote.

The existing `"multiple trailers returns first"` case is unchanged (both trailers are in the real block).

Proposed title:

```text
fix(checkpoints): trust only final trailer blocks for mutations
```

Proposed body:

```markdown
Refs #2168

PR #2168 prevents untrusted commit subjects from forging Entire trailers, but deliberately leaves commit-body handling to a separate change. Mutation paths still treated an `Entire-Checkpoint` line anywhere in a commit message as authority to select an existing checkpoint.

That allowed checkpoint-shaped body text to redirect PostCommit condensation, session attachment, generated explanations, or legacy migration. At the same time, read-only history discovery must continue recognizing embedded trailers from squash merges.

## Make the trailer block the mutation boundary

This change adds strict final-trailer-block parsing and uses it wherever a checkpoint may be created, reused, reconciled, or modified:

- commit preparation and amendment
- PostCommit condensation
- session attachment
- `checkpoint explain --generate`
- legacy session migration

Whole-message parsing remains available for read-only checkpoint discovery, preserving squash-merge history behavior.

The strict parser follows Git trailer structure: leading whitespace cannot turn body text into a trailer, while indented continuation lines remain supported.

Commit-message cleanup now also follows Git configuration. Editor flows honor `core.commentString`, `core.commentChar`, and `auto`; messages supplied through `-m` or `-F` preserve comment-prefixed user content.

## Verification

- `mise run lint` — 0 issues
- `mise run test` — 10,375 passed, 8 skipped
- `mise run test:integration` — 562 passed, 5 skipped
- `mise run test:ci` — passed, including Vogon and Roger-Roger canaries
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`

Regression tests exercise the durable PostCommit and attach boundaries, generated explanation paths, legacy migration, Git comment configuration, indented pseudo-trailers, continuation lines, and preserved squash-history discovery.
```

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

name: create-pr
description: Draft, then create or report a ready-for-review or draft pull request for the current branch with a reviewer-oriented explanation of the problem, fix, trade-offs, scope, and verification. Use when the user asks to open, raise, create, or draft a PR, after a branch has been checked and pushed.

# Create PR

Draft the review artifact for the current branch, get user approval, then create or report the PR.

## Do

- Check whether a PR already exists for the current branch.
- Summarize the diff against the base branch. When the Entire Graph plugin is installed (`entire graph version` succeeds), `entire graph diff --base <base> --head HEAD --json` gives the entity-level change list — the changed functions and types to build the reviewer-facing story around, instead of reconstructing it from raw hunks.
- Include tests or checks actually run.
- Keep the title specific to the outcome. Follow the repository's title convention;
  use a conventional-commit prefix only when the repository does.
- Draft the title and PR body first, then ask the user to approve or edit it.
- Only create or update a public PR after the user approves the draft.
- If the user asks for a draft PR, create it as a draft. Do not infer draft status
  merely because the body is being drafted for approval.
- Return the PR URL.

## Body Style

Write a reviewer-facing argument, not a changelog or a fixed form. A reviewer
should be able to understand the failure or need, why the chosen boundary is the
right one, what behavior changes, and how the claims were verified.

Use this as a flexible shape, not a required template:

```markdown
<Optional relationship line: Closes #123, Refs #123, or a trail/design link>

<A concrete opening paragraph stating the problem and the outcome.>

## <The bug | Problem | Why the existing guard did not help>

<Evidence and the causal chain. Name the prior behavior precisely.>

## <The fix | What changed | Why this shape>

<Explain the governing design boundary, important behavior, and non-obvious
constraints. Call out deliberate asymmetries or trade-offs when they exist.>

## <Behavior changes | Performance | Compatibility>

<Include only when the change has material user-visible, rollout, API, or
measured performance consequences.>

## Verification

<State what was actually run and what it proved. Include relevant negative or
positive controls, measurements, or an honest reason a check was not run.>

## <Deliberately not included | Known limitation | Follow-ups>

<Use only for concrete scope boundaries that help review this PR.>
```

- Use `Closes` or `Fixes` only when merging the PR really resolves the linked
  issue. Use `Refs` or a plain link for context or partial work.
- Choose headings that carry the PR's actual argument. Prefer specific headings
  such as `Why the gate did not stop it`, `The fix`, or `The trade, made
  deliberately` over generic buckets such as `Core Changes` and `API Notes`.

const title = "fix(checkpoints): trust only final trailer blocks for mutations";
const body = `Refs #2168

PR #2168 prevents untrusted commit subjects from forging Entire trailers, but deliberately leaves commit-body handling to a separate change. Mutation paths still treated an \`Entire-Checkpoint\` line anywhere in a commit message as authority to select an existing checkpoint.

That allowed checkpoint-shaped body text to redirect PostCommit condensation, session attachment, generated explanations, or legacy migration. At the same time, read-only history discovery must continue recognizing embedded trailers from squash merges.

## Make the trailer block the mutation boundary

This change adds strict final-trailer-block parsing and uses it wherever a checkpoint may be created, reused, reconciled, or modified:

- commit preparation and amendment
- PostCommit condensation
- session attachment
- \`checkpoint explain --generate\`
- legacy session migration

Whole-message parsing remains available for read-only checkpoint discovery, preserving squash-merge history behavior.

The strict parser follows Git trailer structure: leading whitespace cannot turn body text into a trailer, while indented continuation lines remain supported.

Commit-message cleanup now also follows Git configuration. Editor flows honor \`core.commentString\`, \`core.commentChar\`, and \`auto\`; messages supplied through \`-m\` or \`-F\` preserve comment-prefixed user content.

## Verification

- \`mise run lint\` — 0 issues
- \`mise run test\` — 10,375 passed, 8 skipped
- \`mise run test:integration\` — 562 passed, 5 skipped
- \`mise run test:ci\` — passed, including Vogon and Roger-Roger canaries
- \`git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check\`

Regression tests exercise the durable PostCommit and attach boundaries, generated explanation paths, legacy migration, Git comment configuration, indented pseudo-trailers, continuation lines, and preserved squash-history discovery.`;
const shellQuote = s => "'" + s.replaceAll("'", "'\"'\"'") + "'";
const cmd = [
  "gh pr create",
  "--repo", shellQuote("entireio/cli"),
  "--base", shellQuote("main"),
  "--head", shellQuote("MuskanPaliwal:fix-checkpoint-trailer-block"),
  "--draft",
  "--title", shellQuote(title),
  "--body", shellQuote(body)
].join(" ");
const r = await tools.exec_command({
  cmd,
  workdir: "/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block",
  sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated",
  justification: "May I create the approved draft pull request in entireio/cli?",
  prefix_rule: ["gh", "pr", "create"],
  yield_time_ms: 30000,
  max_output_tokens: 8000
});
text(JSON.stringify(r));
